observation_summary: The HashCodeBuilder used a ThreadLocal registry that was never cleaned up, causing memory leaks in container environments and failing to properly manage the lifecycle of the registry set.
reasoning_summary: The fix involves changing the lifecycle management of the ThreadLocal registry. Specifically, it changes how the registry is initialized (lazy initialization instead of eager), how it is checked for existence (null checks), and crucially, it adds logic to remove the ThreadLocal entry when the registry becomes empty. This is a procedural change to the algorithm managing the registry's lifecycle, ensuring it is cleaned up properly to prevent memory leaks. It is not a simple missing guard (Checking) because it involves a fundamental change to the lifecycle management strategy of the shared resource.
evidence_used: The fix adds synchronization and explicit removal of the ThreadLocal entry when the registry is empty.
The fix changes the initialization of the ThreadLocal from an eager initialValue() to a lazy approach.
The fix adds null checks for the registry in isRegistered and unregister methods.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix adds null checks, the core issue is the lack of a cleanup mechanism for the ThreadLocal, which is a procedural/algorithmic lifecycle management problem.
The fix adds synchronization, but this is to protect the lazy initialization of the registry, not to fix a race condition or serialization order issue.
